select.hypothesis: A standardized-feature multinomial logistic regression with L2 regularization and C selected by stratified cross-validated negative log loss will produce well-calibrated class probabilities for the 99 leaf classes and outperform unregularized or poorly scaled linear classifiers.

A class-conditional Gaussian model with shrinkage on standardized margin, shape, and texture features can capture correlated within-class feature structure and provide better-calibrated probabilities than a diagonal or standard linear model for this high-dimensional multiclass task.

The flat 99-class multinomial logistic model treats all leaf classes as exchangeable and must learn separate boundaries for many closely related species. Deriving a genus-level hierarchy from the target column names and fitting a two-stage regularized multinomial logistic model, first at genus level and then conditionally within genus for species, can share regularization and calibration across related classes; final class probabilities are normalized products of genus and within-genus species probabilities.

Because linear L2 regularization on standardized raw features may underfit nonlinear class boundaries, a low-rank kernel approximation such as Nystroem/RBF followed by strongly regularized multinomial logistic regression can model interactions among margin, shape, and texture features while preserving calibrated multiclass probabilities.
